payload.vision_scope_stated: Complete. Vision inherits se.vision with the delta stated, and the rewalk ADDS what the first pass could not know: the review rounds were themselves written-but-never-collected. Goal system: G1-G4 inherited, G5 ADDED and ruled FIRST - a review happens because something asks for it. To-be world gains the gate that reviews itself and the reopen that does something. Scope is now three halves, with Half C (the review actually happens) leading because it is already built and green. Non-goals: fourteen, each one line.
payload.problem_agreed:
KILLER. The delta is real, measured, and the rewalk made it sharper rather than softer.

MEASURED, unchanged: 4131 calls; se_file_patch most-used at 645 and most-failing at 28, applying one edit per call; six se_help misses across three days on reading and searching, the one demand never served while every other was built within days; a porting law that mandates two sources the lane could not open.

WHAT THE REWALK ADDS, and it is worth more than the tools: se.meth-gate-review has required verify / validate / redteam / verdict since it was written; no evidence form ever collected them; NOT ONE has been filled in any gate of any iteration in this project. The method even explains the mechanism in its own text - 'the compiler will inject the standard fields; until then, fill them from here' - and nothing ever did.

THE COST IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. This iteration's own first pass wrote R3 ('a match carries the caller's requested surrounding lines'), chose a provider that cannot do it, minted an ADR explaining why context belongs elsewhere, wrote tests against the DESIGN rather than the REGISTER, and passed a gate green. The owner caught it by reading. A verify round is literally 'each input state's evidence read against its claim' - it would have caught it in one line.

AND THE DEFECT HAS THREE LEVELS, which is what makes it worth an iteration rather than a fix: items are prose so conformance cannot be linted; guidance is prose in a state note so rules never reach the packet; and the review was prose in a method note so the review never happened. Each level was written, none collected. The top level is the one that catches the other two.

WORTH HAVING: yes, and the counter-argument deserves its answer. 'This is a day on tools, not product.' Without it every future iteration pays the same tax AND every self-blessed killer keeps resting on a review that has never once occurred. The owner's own words this afternoon - 'who checks that? why is there a requirement and then you violate it and nobody sees that?' - is the problem statement.
payload.prior_art_positioned:
SCANNED at frame_delta and CORRECTED here by the owner.

THE FIELD: three layers of code search with sequential escalation (exact / structural / semantic); offset-limit paging with refuse-and-redirect; results capped and typed. Positioned: adopt exact, reject semantic on FRESHNESS (an index tolerates staleness; this agent reads back what it just wrote), defer structural with a trigger, keep BM25 where it belongs on ledger prose.

THE CORRECTION, which reverses the first pass's conclusion: I argued that composing two search tools was itself the duplication our no-duplicate-code rule forbids. The owner: THESE ARE TWO JOBS, NOT ONE. Searching a working tree and searching history are different questions; one tool per job is fit, not duplication. So the positioning is COMPOSITION - ripgrep for the tree, git for the record - and the first pass talked itself out of half of a correct design.

v1 IS THE PRIOR ART FOR THE OTHER HALF, and it is prior art we own and had not read: its milestone-review guide carries the whole rubric - increasing scrutiny, the two sets (the gate's own checks AND every input check feeding it), 'a bless is not proof', 'cite a rubric not vibes', 'a significant decision carries a kill-criterion', 'log the override WITH its dissent', 'the agent never self-certifies a killer gate'. v2 cited that rubric at meth-gate-review and never carried it. It is now ported as se.meth-review-rounds, with the two clauses we deliberately do NOT take (the M4 diagram hard-rule and its boilerplate question) recorded as omissions rather than dropped.

UNPOSITIONED, and I would rather say so than claim novelty: nothing in the scanned field addresses whether a gate's own review happens. Either that is genuinely unaddressed or we looked in the wrong place.
payload.success_measurable:
Twelve needs with pass lines. N1-N9 inherited; N2 CORRECTED; N10-N12 added.

N2 IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. It read 'a known line is located in ONE call' - which the first pass satisfied while violating R3, because locating is not the same as returning context. It now reads: located in one call AND the result carries the caller's requested surrounding lines. The pass line names what the requirement asks for, so no design can meet it by redefining it.

ADDED: N10 a gate is REVIEWED, not just filled - pass line: no gate submittable without all four rounds, enforced by the form, with a mechanical check asserting every gate carries them as required. N11 a reopen verdict does something - pass line: reopen re-activates the cone, supersedes prior fills, and leaves the evidence readable. N12 the red-team is adversarial not decorative - pass line: every redteam_round names a kill-criterion; recorded as the WEAKEST pass line here, since it constrains form and not sincerity.

SIGNALS THAT CANNOT BE SELF-SERVED, measured NEXT iteration: workarounds per iteration, re-derivations of existing rulings, owner rounds per gate - and now a fourth: rounds that changed nothing.

FAILURE CONDITION, stated so it can be quoted back: if the lint sweep produces prose instead of lints, or if the rounds produce agreement instead of scrutiny, this iteration failed however much tooling ships.
payload.risks_logged:
Register open. Four from the first pass, eleven carried from i8d, TWO added by the rewalk.

se.raid-mandatory-rounds-degrade-into-ceremony (risk, agent) - the new central risk. A required field can be satisfied with a paragraph of agreement, and a red-team that restates the case FOR the decision is worse than none: same cost, a record that looks like scrutiny, a gate harder to challenge because it appears already challenged. Ruled mitigation from v1's rubric: name the kill-criterion and report what looking for it found. Retro tripwire: count rounds that changed nothing.

se.raid-reopen-can-erase-work-by-cone (risk, agent) - reopen takes the whole downstream cone; this rewalk superseded 30 fills across 46 states in one call. Mitigated by design (supersede, never delete), so the cost is re-walking and never the record.

AND ONE CARRIED ENTRY IS NOW THE MOST IMPORTANT IN THE REGISTER: se.raid-items-are-prose-so-the-best-checks-cannot-be-mechanical, because the rewalk showed it is the same disease at three levels rather than one gap.
payload.verify_round:
BUILT IT RIGHT - each input state since M0 read against its claim, not summarised from memory.

draft_vision: claims to inherit se.vision plus a delta. VERIFIED - it points at the resident vision and states only what changed, and the added G5 is traceable to a measured finding rather than an opinion.
define_actual: claims eleven pains with witnesses. VERIFIED by opening the witnesses: pains 1-8 carry log measurements and owner quotes from today; pains 9-11 carry three I ran myself - meth-gate-review's own text (read in full), the R3-versus-implementation comparison, and a grep showing 'reopen' appears zero times in the engine.
log_risks: claims two new entries with kind, owner, trigger. VERIFIED - both exist as nodes, both carry a concrete fallback rather than 'monitor'.
frame_delta: claims a corrected gap and twelve needs with pass lines. VERIFIED, and this is where the verify round earned itself: N2's OLD pass line ('located in ONE call') would have passed against the first pass's locations-only design, which VIOLATES R3. The pass line was the hole, not the design alone. Corrected here.
scope_non_goals: claims three halves and fourteen non-goals. VERIFIED - Half C is not a promise but a fact: the injection is committed to the worktree and its guard passes 4/4 (run-947a9e7ecfcf).
pressure_test: claims seven hostile questions with two folded findings. VERIFIED - the sweep question is genuinely unanswered and is recorded as owed rather than answered.

ONE INPUT I CANNOT FULLY VERIFY, stated rather than waved: the log measurements (645 calls, 28 failures, 4131 total) come from se_log_query runs I read, but I did not independently recount them. They are engine output, not my arithmetic.
payload.validate_round:
BUILT THE RIGHT THING - against the frame, the vision, and the register rather than against this iteration's own plan.

AGAINST THE VISION: se.vision wants a system whose gates are worth trusting. Half C serves that directly. Halves A and B serve the agent's speed, which is instrumental. The ordering in scope now reflects that, where the first pass led with tools.

AGAINST THE REGISTER: this is where the round bites. Reading R1-R29 against the current state - R3 IS STILL VIOLATED IN THE BUILT CODE. engine/search.ts returns locations only; se.adr-locate-and-read-are-separate is still live; the i12 test suite still contains NO context test. The rewalk has corrected the pass line and the ADR is marked for retirement, but the CODE has not changed yet. I am recording that plainly at the gate where it is true rather than letting the corrected prose imply a corrected implementation.

WHAT NO CHECK COVERS, hunted deliberately: (a) nothing verifies that a method note's required fields actually appear in the form that should collect them - the sweep question, now owed; (b) nothing measures whether a round changed anything, so ceremony is detectable only by a human at a retro; (c) N12's pass line constrains the FORM of the red-team and nothing constrains its honesty.

OUT OF SCOPE BUT ASKED FOR: the owner asked for a full rewalk. That is happening. The owner also asked, earlier, that the search decision be revisited against prior art - done, reversed, and the reversal is recorded.
payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, argued before endorsing, against the criteria rather than by feel.

KILL-CRITERION, named first so it can be looked for: THIS GATE SHOULD FAIL IF THE MOTIVATION IS PROCEDURAL RATHER THAN REAL - that is, if the problem is 'the agent was careless' rather than a defect in the system. A motivation that reduces to 'try harder' does not deserve an iteration.

I LOOKED FOR IT. The strongest version of the case against: 'You are dressing up your own negligence as a system defect. The rounds were documented. A diligent agent would have read meth-gate-review, seen five required fields, and filled them. The state-of-the-art scan was in the guidance you read at that very state. Nothing stopped you.'

That is a real argument and it is PARTLY RIGHT. I read write_requirements' guidance, which names the scan in plain words, and did not perform it. No mechanism prevented me; attention did.

WHY IT DOES NOT KILL THE GATE: the same failure occurred across THREE independent mechanisms, in TWO iterations, and - the decisive fact - in every gate of every iteration in the project's history, including ones walked before this session. A failure mode with that distribution is not a person being careless; it is a system where compliance depends on someone re-reading a linked note at the right moment and no artifact ever asks. The method note itself predicted the fix ('the compiler will inject...'), which means the designers already knew diligence was the wrong enforcement layer.

SECOND OPPOSING CASE: 'G5 above G2 is wrong - lints are objective, rounds are prose, so you have ranked the softer mechanism higher.' Considered seriously. Rejected on this iteration's own evidence: the failure that reached the owner (R3) was NOT lintable - no lint we could build would know that a design satisfies a requirement's letter while defeating its purpose. Reading the register against the work is the only check that catches it, and that is a round.

WHERE I REMAIN EXPOSED, no override needed but recorded: the red-team is written by the agent that wrote the decision. That circularity is real, is logged as se.raid-mandatory-rounds-degrade-into-ceremony, and is not solved here.

NO OVERRIDE IS TAKEN AT THIS GATE - every acceptance item is met on its own terms.
payload.verdict:
PASS.

All five acceptance items met with real evidence; the three rounds ran and two of them changed something (verify corrected N2's pass line; validate surfaced that R3 is still violated in the BUILT CODE and recorded it rather than letting corrected prose imply corrected code).

NOT a clean pass in the sense of nothing outstanding: R3's violation is live in engine/search.ts and se.adr-locate-and-read-are-separate is still on the books. Both are carried FORWARD as work rather than blocking here, because this gate adjudicates the MOTIVATION and the motivation is stronger for the violation existing, not weaker. They must be fixed before gate_architecture, and the architecture gate is where a reopen verdict belongs if they are not.

No states reopened by this verdict.
